text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition parties urge the authorities to open tightly controlled state media ahead of the June 5 parliamentary elections.
- Four new newspapers, Demain l'Algerie, Al Alam, La Nouvelle Republique and Saout al Ahrar, to appear soon in Algeria's newstands.

- The interior ministry orders political parties to change names and manifestos in line with a newly adopted law which provides for politicians to steer clear of using the Moslem faith and the country's Arab and Berber languages to gain power. The Algerian Renewal Party (PRA), the Rally for Democracy and Culture (RCD) and the former ruling National Liberation Front (FLN) say their foundations and acronyms are conform to the law.

- Party leaders mull over forging alliances to compete for the legislative elections. The Call for Peace group, seeking dialogue between opposition, including Islamists, and the government to end violence, said it will field candidates backed by several political parties. The anti-Islamist RCD urges secular forces to agree on common candidates to "block the way" for Islamist candidates.
- The government collects 37 billion dinars ($660 million) tax in 1996.
- Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf visits Brussels to boost ties with Belguim. ($1 = 56 dinars)
